---
title: "Measuring coverage bias"
---

Coverage compares active users with the population of each area. Keep the same
geography and counting period in both columns. A user count is the denominator
for an inverse-penetration weight; it should describe the population represented
by the observed data.

```python
from debiaspy import debiaspy_example_data, measure_bias, measure_bias_distribution

bundle = debiaspy_example_data(n_areas=25)
coverage = bundle["coverage"]
print(measure_bias(coverage).head())
print(measure_bias_distribution(coverage)["summary"])
```

`measure_bias` returns coverage scores and bias values. Distribution summaries
compare each area's share of population with its share of active users. Read
[input definitions](../inputs.md) before using the Census demonstration's
OD-margin-derived counts as independent population coverage evidence.
